intent: Let the owner withdraw a proposed element, so it leaves the draft.

edit.summary:
I added a `withdraw_element` action to `authoring/authoring.domain.yaml`. It lets the owner withdraw a proposed element so it leaves the draft. I haven't run any checks or the scenarios on the result.

- **New state:** `Element.review` now has a `withdrawn` value.
- **Action:** `withdraw_element` is owner-only and targets an Element. It's marked `status: proposed` because the request has no interview or record source to cite.
- **Element transitions:** A proposed element moves to `withdrawn`. A confirmed element refuses it, with the same reason `mark_unknown` gives: change it by a new proposal and commit. An unknown element has it set to n/a. The new `withdrawn` row has every action set to n/a, so a withdrawn element is final.
- **Version:** I bumped the file version from 16 to 17.

Withdrawal only changes the element's review state. I didn't add a kernel call that physically removes it from the working copy, because no such call is declared. If you want the draft file itself edited, that needs a kernel call, which I'd have to invent.

I left `delivery` and the composition alone. I also didn't add a scenario for the new action.

findings.problem: withdraw_element has no effects, so it only flips Element.review to withdrawn. Nothing calls the kernel or removes the element from the working copy. Every other action that changes the draft calls the kernel (propose_element, confirm_element). The stated goal, that the element leaves the draft, is not met: the proposed value stays in the declaration and only the review label changes.

confirm_all_proposed confirms elements through the kernel with paths 'all'. A withdrawn element is still in the working copy, so it can be confirmed there, and record_confirmation would then be reported for an element the model holds as withdrawn. The withdrawn state is also n/a for record_confirmation. The kernel's confirmation and the review state can disagree.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml, actions.confirm_all_proposed and the Element transitions for withdrawn

findings.problem: An element marked unknown cannot be withdrawn (unknown.withdraw_element is n/a). The request says marking unknown keeps noise in the draft, yet an unknown element has no way out of the draft and stays visible forever. Only proposed elements can be withdrawn.

withdrawn is a new terminal state, but the glossary entries for element, draft and unknown do not mention it. The unknown entry says an element stays visible until someone answers it, and there is now a second way for an element to leave. The world fixtures and scenarios do not exercise withdraw_element at all, including the allowed path from proposed and the denied path from confirmed.

The Element review enum gained a value and the Authoring actions and states changed, but the interface the composition pins stays at `interface: 1`. Delivery and other consumers get no signal that a new review state exists.

withdraw_element has no effects. It does not call the kernel to remove the element from the working copy, and no reply records a removal. Nothing in the declaration makes the element leave the draft. It only sets review to withdrawn, and the Draft declaration still holds it. The stated goal is that the element leaves the draft, and this change does not do that.

confirm_all_proposed calls the kernel's confirm_element with paths 'all', which confirms every element still proposed in the working copy. A withdrawn element is still in the working copy, so it can be confirmed through that path. That is the opposite of what withdrawing means. It also bypasses the matrix, where confirm_element from withdrawn is n/a. The action's description and the 'only-a-person-element-confirmed' rule were not revisited.

An element marked unknown cannot be withdrawn (unknown.withdraw_element is n/a). The stated reason is that marking wrong proposals unknown keeps noise in the draft. Those wrong elements are exactly the ones already marked unknown, and they stay in the draft, so the problem is only partly solved. The glossary says unknown 'stays visible until someone answers it', which leaves no way to remove one.

A DecisionRequest links to an Element, and an open request can exist for an element that is then withdrawn (DR1 on E1 in the fixtures, for example). Nothing closes or invalidates that request. The owner can still be asked, and can still decide, about an element that no longer exists in the draft.

The new state and action are not reflected elsewhere in the declaration. The glossary has no entry for withdrawn, and the 'element' glossary entry still describes only drafted and confirmed. No scenario or fixture covers the withdraw paths: withdrawing a proposed element, denial on a confirmed element, or a withdrawn element being terminal. The withdraw_element action and its proposed-to-withdrawn transition are also both status proposed with no source or quote.

The request is to make a withdrawn element leave the draft. But withdraw_element only moves the Element's review field to 'withdrawn'. It has no effect that calls the kernel to remove the element from the working copy, unlike propose_element, confirm_element and the other draft-changing actions, which all call the kernel. The element's path and value would stay in the declaration and in the next commit, so the noise the change is meant to remove stays in the draft.

An element marked unknown cannot be withdrawn (withdraw_element is n/a in the unknown row). The change request says marking a wrong proposal unknown 'keeps noise in the draft', and the glossary says an unknown element 'stays visible until someone answers it'. So a wrong proposal that was already marked unknown can never leave the draft; only a proposed element can be withdrawn.

No scenario covers the new behaviour: withdrawing a proposed element, being denied on a confirmed one, or having no further actions on a withdrawn one. The new action, state and matrix cells are marked proposed and are untested. The world fixtures also have no withdrawn element.

withdraw_element only moves the Element's review field to 'withdrawn'. It has no effect that calls the kernel, unlike confirm_element and propose_element, which both do. The change request says the element should leave the draft, but the working copy still holds it, and the next commit would snapshot it.

confirm_all_proposed calls the kernel with paths 'all', which acts on the working copy and not on the review field. A withdrawn element is still in the working copy, so it can be confirmed anyway. The action's description, 'every element still proposed', no longer matches what happens.

An open DecisionRequest links to an Element, and nothing handles a request whose element is later withdrawn. The request stays open and the owner is still asked to decide about an element that no longer exists in the draft.
findings.where: authoring.domain.yaml, links.element (DecisionRequest to Element) and transitions.DecisionRequest

findings.problem: A withdrawn element is terminal and withdraw_element is n/a for 'unknown'. An element wrongly marked unknown therefore cannot be removed from the draft, and it stays visible until someone answers it. This leaves the noise the change was meant to remove. Elsewhere, 'unknown' elements are expected to stay visible.
record_proposal is n/a for 'withdrawn'. If the kernel's reply to propose_element arrives after the owner withdraws, the reply is rejected by the matrix. No handling is declared for that case.

The change adds a new review state and a new action but no scenario for withdrawing and no withdrawn fixture. The glossary and the element description do not mention 'withdrawn'. The 'confirmed' deny and the 'unknown' n/a paths for withdraw are untested.

withdraw_element only moves the Element's review field to 'withdrawn'. It has no effects or kernel call, unlike confirm_element, which calls confirm_element to write to the working copy. Nothing removes the element from the draft declaration, so the stated goal that it 'leaves the draft' is not met. The element stays in the draft file and the commit snapshot while the model marks it withdrawn.

An element already marked unknown cannot be withdrawn (the unknown row sets withdraw_element to n/a). The request exists because unknown 'keeps noise in the draft', and unknown elements stay visible until answered. A wrong proposal that was marked unknown therefore has no way out of the draft.

Kernel replies are set to n/a in the withdrawn state. propose_element asynchronously replies with record_proposal, and record_proposal is n/a for withdrawn. If the owner withdraws before the kernel replies, the reply hits a forbidden cell and the issues/issue_summary record is lost or errors.

The glossary and the Element description still say elements are only proposed or confirmed, and the 'unknown' entry still says unknown elements stay visible until answered. Neither mentions the new withdrawn state or that a proposed element can now leave the draft.

No scenario or fixture covers withdrawal. There is no withdrawn Element in the world, no scenario that withdraws a proposed element, and none that checks the denial for a confirmed one. The new cells and the deny rule are unverified, and the new state is unreachable from the fixtures.
